# SakanaAI/AI-Scientist — pinned source assessment

**Source:** https://github.com/SakanaAI/AI-Scientist at [`1de1dbc1f4ee2c5f61e9c94348d55eb51d7fa2eb`](https://github.com/SakanaAI/AI-Scientist/commit/1de1dbc1f4ee2c5f61e9c94348d55eb51d7fa2eb) (committed 2025-12-19). The ignored checkout at `references/work/sakana-ai-scientist/` was removed after release; it was never a runtime dependency. This is an external technique source, not evidence of Google's Co-Scientist implementation.

## Terms and reuse boundary

The pinned root [LICENSE](https://github.com/SakanaAI/AI-Scientist/blob/1de1dbc1f4ee2c5f61e9c94348d55eb51d7fa2eb/LICENSE) is **The AI Scientist Source Code License**, version 1.0 (December 2025), not MIT. It grants conditional reproduction, derivative-work, and distribution rights. Distribution of the contribution requires the full license, and its restrictions and downstream terms include a prominent AI-generation disclosure for scientific manuscripts, papers, or technical reports produced using that software. The tracked tree contains no second `LICENSE`, `COPYING`, or `NOTICE` file. A bundled [Tensorf helper](https://github.com/SakanaAI/AI-Scientist/blob/1de1dbc1f4ee2c5f61e9c94348d55eb51d7fa2eb/templates/tensorf/dataLoader/colmap2nerf.py#L3-L9) separately reserves NVIDIA's rights and prohibits use, reproduction, or distribution without an express agreement. No bundled template, source, or prompt is approved for copying. Independently implemented techniques require a distinct local acceptance case and source-idea attribution.

## Source shape and operating assumptions

The checkout has 2,326 tracked files: 15 under `ai_scientist/`, 25 under `review_ai_scientist/`, 1,028 under `review_iclr_bench/`, 1,107 example-paper artifacts, and 136 template files. No tracked Python test module matches the repository's `test*.py` or `tests/` pattern; the benchmark and example artifacts require separate inspection before treating them as validation. The pinned [README](https://github.com/SakanaAI/AI-Scientist/blob/1de1dbc1f4ee2c5f61e9c94348d55eb51d7fa2eb/README.md) describes a Linux/NVIDIA CUDA/PyTorch workflow, LaTeX, code-editing experiments, and frontier-model API credentials. It recommends GPT-4o for review, reports model-specific positive bias and formatting failures, and describes roughly $15 per generated paper. The optional Semantic Scholar key and experimental no-key OpenAlex route do not make the overall workflow free. No upstream setup, agent workflow, model, or benchmark command has been run, and no campaign credential was supplied to the checkout.

The authors' [paper](https://arxiv.org/html/2408.06292v3) reports automated-review performance on 500 ICLR 2022 OpenReview papers (65% versus 66% balanced accuracy in its comparison) and describes 10 novelty-search rounds, 5 review reflections, and 5 ensembled reviews in its experimental setup. It reports that ensembling did not substantially improve accuracy, although it reduced variance, and its calibrated reviewer had a higher false-positive rate than the human comparison (0.31 versus 0.17). The authors also note possible training-data overlap, camera-ready/submission differences, overestimated self-assessed novelty, unfair experimental comparisons, and invented results. These are results and limitations for machine-learning manuscripts, not verified gains in our hypothesis-level scientific workflow. Any local adoption must be evaluated at the appropriate Co-Scientist boundary under the campaign's fixed inputs and zero-cost model policy.

## Implemented architecture and inspection map

The standard [launcher](https://github.com/SakanaAI/AI-Scientist/blob/1de1dbc1f4ee2c5f61e9c94348d55eb51d7fa2eb/launch_scientist.py#L343-L420) generates a template-conditioned idea batch, checks novelty, saves `ideas.json`, runs experiments for selected ideas, writes LaTeX papers, and requests reviews. Idea generation and reflection are prompt-driven in [generate_ideas.py](https://github.com/SakanaAI/AI-Scientist/blob/1de1dbc1f4ee2c5f61e9c94348d55eb51d7fa2eb/ai_scientist/generate_ideas.py#L14-L174). Its [novelty loop](https://github.com/SakanaAI/AI-Scientist/blob/1de1dbc1f4ee2c5f61e9c94348d55eb51d7fa2eb/ai_scientist/generate_ideas.py#L285-L492) asks the model for Semantic Scholar or OpenAlex queries, exposes up to ten search results per query, and eventually asks for a free-form Boolean novelty verdict. It can search repeatedly, but the idea record does not provide a structured per-claim prior-art audit or calibrated novelty score. The experimental open-ended launcher has an [archive-conditioned idea path](https://github.com/SakanaAI/AI-Scientist/blob/1de1dbc1f4ee2c5f61e9c94348d55eb51d7fa2eb/ai_scientist/generate_ideas.py#L178-L272); unlike the standard path, it [does not gate the newest idea on novelty](https://github.com/SakanaAI/AI-Scientist/blob/1de1dbc1f4ee2c5f61e9c94348d55eb51d7fa2eb/experimental/launch_oe_scientist.py#L359-L394). These are distinct shipped paths, not interchangeable claims about a single invariant.

The [experiment executor](https://github.com/SakanaAI/AI-Scientist/blob/1de1dbc1f4ee2c5f61e9c94348d55eb51d7fa2eb/ai_scientist/perform_experiments.py#L12-L165) uses Aider to edit `experiment.py`, executes the revised code as a subprocess, gathers metric means and standard errors, and feeds the results back into planning, plotting, and notes. That requires a writable code template and GPU-oriented local runtime; it is not a general scientific-verification or safety layer. State is primarily per-idea JSON, snapshots, and result folders, without the current product's durable task and append-only lineage contracts. The [reviewer](https://github.com/SakanaAI/AI-Scientist/blob/1de1dbc1f4ee2c5f61e9c94348d55eb51d7fa2eb/ai_scientist/perform_review.py#L126-L243) can sample multiple same-model reviews, aggregate numeric scores through a meta-review, and reflect on the result; the standard launcher [hard-codes GPT-4o](https://github.com/SakanaAI/AI-Scientist/blob/1de1dbc1f4ee2c5f61e9c94348d55eb51d7fa2eb/launch_scientist.py#L263-L280) for this step. Review parsing has a visible [all-invalid-samples failure path](https://github.com/SakanaAI/AI-Scientist/blob/1de1dbc1f4ee2c5f61e9c94348d55eb51d7fa2eb/ai_scientist/perform_review.py#L163-L175); this is an assessment of its contract, not a claim from a live experiment.

Its [ICLR benchmark](https://github.com/SakanaAI/AI-Scientist/blob/1de1dbc1f4ee2c5f61e9c94348d55eb51d7fa2eb/review_iclr_bench/iclr_analysis.py#L170-L205) compares binary Accept/Reject labels with accuracy, F1, hard-label ROC AUC, and false-positive/negative rates. It does not measure biomedical hypothesis novelty, citation support, or scientific correctness. The cached reviews and example papers are artifacts, not a unit-test suite; running the benchmark can invoke paid providers. [Paper writing and citation insertion](https://github.com/SakanaAI/AI-Scientist/blob/1de1dbc1f4ee2c5f61e9c94348d55eb51d7fa2eb/ai_scientist/perform_writeup.py#L220-L487) serve autonomous paper production, which is outside this campaign's product scope. The alternative OpenAlex search record does not supply the `citationStyles` field that this citation-insertion path reads, so the two paths should not be treated as one proven end-to-end connector.

## Comparison with the current product

Our durable run executes independent review and evidence tasks, Elo pairwise ranking, deep verification, recurrent meta-review, and append-only hypothesis lineage ([workflow map](../../docs/EXPLAINER.md), [fan-out](../../app/app/engine_tasks_fanout.py)). This is the **Google-backed requirement** boundary; Sakana's paper-generation pipeline does not alter it. A local literature-tool path [searches once per draft](../../engine/src/co_scientist/agents/generation/literature_tools/validate_novelty.py) and [analyzes papers before synthesis](../../engine/src/co_scientist/agents/generation/literature_tools/validate_stages.py); ordinary review instead explicitly marks its novelty score as [prior-knowledge judgment](../../engine/src/co_scientist/prompts/templates/review.md), without claiming a search. The broader literature review can perform a budgeted follow-up search, and deep reviews gather claim-specific evidence, but those do not establish result-conditioned *per-draft* query refinement. Sakana's repeated-query loop is an **external technique** that is only partially covered locally; its terminal Boolean is model-declared, does not expose a per-claim evidence ledger, and turns exhausted search errors into `novel = False`. Making that Boolean an always-on publication gate would be a **local design choice** without supporting evaluation.

Our initial review, mature cascade, one-time blocked-idea recheck, recurrent review, and Elo tournament already yield multiple distinct judgments, while the app persists their artifacts ([review node](../../engine/src/co_scientist/agents/reflection/review.py), [gate](../../engine/src/co_scientist/agents/reflection/review_gate.py), [ranking parity](../../docs/PARITY.md)). Sakana's ensemble resamples the *same model* for a paper Accept/Reject decision; it is neither independent expert voting nor a replacement for the paper-backed Elo system. Its own paper found no material accuracy increase from ensembling. The local `call_llm_json` boundary retries and validates structured output; Sakana's all-invalid review-sample indexing failure is not a reliability pattern to import.

Our simulation review can execute a bounded computational model in an available sandbox, and a researcher can append measured outcomes with protocol, conditions, controls, interpretation, and evidence IDs ([simulation](../../engine/src/co_scientist/agents/reflection/simulation_execution.py), [outcome store](../../app/app/store/outcomes.py)). Outcomes are visible after publication, but current [report assembly](../../app/app/report_build.py) does not feed them to the engine; the run is not automatically restarted from a new outcome. Sakana's feedback is from edits to its *own* `experiment.py` and template-specific metrics, followed by autonomous replanning. Importing that behavior would add the separate computational-discovery runtime this campaign excludes. The local evolution and meta-review already condition new hypotheses on prior hypothesis/review state; archive-conditioned proposal alone is covered. Autonomous LaTeX paper production is out of scope; the existing report has provenance and safety gates.

No M7 candidate is accepted for code changes. The two tested retrieval alternatives missed all three frozen prior-art targets; the broader result-conditioned technique remains open as M11-NOV-01. The other source mechanisms are already covered, rejected on cited evidence, or outside the authorized product boundary. This is a no-product-change M7 release, not a final rejection of every possible result-conditioned search algorithm. Verify the unchanged deployment rather than forcing a redundant deployment. The source's positive review metrics and novelty verdicts are not local scientific-quality evidence.

## M7-NOV-01 fixed-input preparation

The existing evaluation datasets are synthetic claim/answer cases without a linked real-paper identifier, and the campaign's public retrieval probe verified one DOI by querying its known title/ID rather than a hypothesis. The retained golden-run summary has public papers but no draft-to-prior-art mapping. None is a valid three-pair retrieval-recall set. Before probing the baseline, the campaign must freeze three public hypothesis/paper pairs with DOI or PMID and a source passage establishing the prior work; record the exact hypothesis wording, source, query cap, tool configuration, and expected identifier. Only then measure whether the current first query retrieves the known prior art and whether a result-conditioned follow-up adds it.

The prospective input set is now frozen in [`sakana/novelty-inputs-v1.json`](sakana/novelty-inputs-v1.json), SHA-256 `e226b891f26f13870ad974726fa2b0d625ddcd4c91696c10bced794771e30bf7`. It selects three public papers across neurodegeneration, virology, and tumor immunology, with exact PMID/DOI targets and paraphrased source anchors from their primary abstracts. All wording and identifiers were fixed before any of these drafts was submitted to the product retrieval path. The baseline uses the existing `pubmed_search_with_fulltext` MCP interface, `draft_hypothesis[:200]`, and `max_papers=3`, with no model calls and an isolated cache. A hit means the exact target identifier is among those three results. [NCBI describes E-utilities as a free public service](https://ncbiinsights.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/2017/11/02/new-api-keys-for-the-e-utilities/), with a [three-request-per-second unauthenticated limit](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK25497/); the isolated probe stayed below it and passed no API key or ambient credentials.

The live baseline on 2026-09-23 is [`sakana/novelty-baseline-v1.json`](sakana/novelty-baseline-v1.json): **0/3 exact target-paper hits**, with zero returned papers for each draft and no tool errors. [`sakana/novelty_probe.py`](sakana/novelty_probe.py) called the existing `MCPToolClient` and `pubmed_search_with_fulltext` with the frozen query rule and cap, recording only identifiers/titles rather than article bodies. The reference MCP server and client ran with `env -i`, a fresh `/tmp/coscientist-m7-novelty-baseline/` home/cache, `PYTHON_DOTENV_DISABLED=1`, `COSCIENTIST_REQUIRE_FREE_MODELS=1`, an explicitly qualified loopback `/mcp` endpoint, and one ephemeral local shared secret. No API key, account-backed retrieval, or model inference entered either process. Two initial client admissions failed locally before any tool call because the endpoint and then secret were omitted; those are setup failures, not trials. The qualified run succeeded; the server was stopped afterward. These three empty results reproduce a concrete retrieval gap, but do not yet establish that Sakana-style result-conditioned search is the best correction. The local main literature-review path already has a query-broadening helper, so reuse must be checked before a new loop is built.

The existing [`broadened_queries`](../../engine/src/co_scientist/agents/generation/literature_review/query_broadening.py) assumes its input is already a keyword query with meaningful leading terms. On the frozen prose drafts, its shortest variants were `In motor`, `SARS-CoV-2 may`, and `In checkpoint-treated`; these discard the mechanism. The existing [`_distill_goal_to_query`](../../engine/src/co_scientist/agents/generation/literature_review/queries.py) caps at eight early non-stopwords, losing `STMN2` in the neurodegeneration case and `NKG2A` in the tumor case. A **local design choice** was tested: extract digit-bearing identifiers and uppercase abbreviations from anywhere in a draft, add context up to eight terms/200 characters, and apply `broadened_queries` for at most two retries after a successfully empty first query. The red validator test reproduced the missing retry (`KeyError` after the empty result); 33 related tests and Ruff then passed with the trial implementation. It preserved configured parameter mapping, shared slug, run ID, source IDs, error propagation, and the no-config skip. This was an experiment, not copied Sakana code.

The matched configured-path live comparison used the same frozen input hash, PubMed MCP tool, three-paper cap, parameter mapper/parser, and separate credential-empty home/caches for each arm. [`sakana/novelty-paired-baseline-v1.json`](sakana/novelty-paired-baseline-v1.json) records **0/3 target hits in three MCP calls**; [`sakana/novelty-paired-candidate-v1.json`](sakana/novelty-paired-candidate-v1.json) records **0/3 in six MCP calls**. All three candidate keyword searches returned three source-ID-bearing papers, but none had the predeclared target PMID/DOI. There were no tool errors, model calls, paid accounts, or metered tools. MCP-call counts are not a count of internal Entrez/PMC requests. An independent probe review identified that a retrieval-only, target-positive set cannot establish false-rejection non-regression for genuinely distinct ideas or downstream report provenance; no such claim is made. The candidate did not meet the primary metric, so its product code and tests were reverted. The retained JSON records the exact requests and returned IDs, but the unretained candidate script is not presented as a maintained product interface.

The local PubMed source requests IDs with [`sort="pub_date"`](../../engine/mcp_server/pubmed_client.py), then selects up to three papers, favoring PMC fulltext. This explains why a broad query can surface recent related papers while missing an older known prior-art target; it does not by itself prove relevance sorting would improve the product. A read-only NCBI ESearch probe using each candidate's eight-term keyword query with relevance sorting returned zero IDs. A narrower anchor query found the SARS-CoV-2 target at rank 1 and the STMN2 target at rank 4, while the Qa-1b target was absent from the top nine; those are exploratory source observations, not candidate acceptance or engine-boundary results. M7-NOV-01 stays open for a relevance-aware or result-conditioned approach with a predeclared comparison. No failed retry code was retained.

## M7-NOV-01c source choice before live calls

[OpenAlex's current official pricing](https://help.openalex.org/access/pricing/) meters search requests after a $1/day free account allowance, with prepaid funds used after the allowance; its [search documentation](https://help.openalex.org/api/searching/) says results are relevance ranked. The campaign cannot verify that an existing account-backed key would stop at the free allowance, so OpenAlex search is excluded from this zero-additional-spend experiment even though the local tool remains configured for ordinary users. This is a current external operating constraint, not evidence about Google's implementation.

[Europe PMC's public REST documentation](https://europepmc.org/RestfulWebService) states that search defaults to relevance ordering. The existing [`search_europepmc`](../../engine/mcp_server/tools/lit_review/europepmc_search.py) uses that REST endpoint without an account key, returns source-stamped records with DOI/PMID, and is already declared in the local tool registry. [`sakana/novelty-source-plan-v1.json`](sakana/novelty-source-plan-v1.json) freezes a three-case source viability test before querying it: original prose as an ablation, and the first three biomedical anchor terms from each frozen draft as the primary query, both capped at three results. The anchor terms are copied from the leading terms of the prior rejected candidate's recorded requests; no known target ID, DOI, title, or author enters a query. A target-recall gain over 0/3 plus intact source IDs and no errors would justify a product-boundary candidate, not adoption by itself. Decision-safety and provenance checks would still be required; if recall remains 0/3 this source/query combination is rejected without changing production code.

The live MCP probe [`sakana/novelty-source-results-v1.json`](sakana/novelty-source-results-v1.json) used an isolated, credential-empty server and client with the campaign free-mode guard. The three unchanged-prose ablations returned no target; the first two anchor queries also returned no target. The third anchor query failed: the client artifact records a parse error, while the retained [server log excerpt](sakana/novelty-source-503-v1.txt) records Europe PMC's HTTP 503 for that exact request. One later retry of **only** the failed query returned normally and also missed the target ([`sakana/novelty-source-retry-v1.json`](sakana/novelty-source-retry-v1.json)). Across the three successful primary calls the exact target recall is **0/3**; source IDs were retained, PMID/DOI values were retained where supplied, and no model or account-backed call occurred. The predeclared stop rule rejects this source/query combination. Because it does not improve the primary metric, no workflow integration or claim about downstream false-rejection safety is justified. [`sakana/novelty_source_probe.py`](sakana/novelty_source_probe.py) records the identifier-only calls and fixture/plan hashes.

## Release and architecture after M7

[PR #30](https://github.com/guy915/Co-Scientist/pull/30) merged the assessment as `53a991713b8091eeb0fdbd642f563b89367b623c`. This release changes no product code, dependency, model route, or deployment configuration. Railway API deployment `cbf25725-c1b0-42c7-a428-993dad838e4a` and MCP deployment `2fdf14a0-e9be-4667-b1bc-c3035b7f83f2` reached SUCCESS on that commit; the Vercel production status was success. The deployed API reported healthy store, engine, queue, and disk checks, and the non-mutating production smoke passed health, MCP availability, ownership isolation, untrusted-origin CORS, and sanitized-share checks. The retained [release record](sakana/m7-release-verification.json) carries exact IDs and limitations. GitHub Actions did not run its jobs because of the account billing hold; the user-authorized hosted-CI exception was used, and no CI pass is claimed.

Architecture remains the existing optional per-draft literature validator, budgeted review research, recurrent review, Elo ranking, and provenance-gated report. No Sakana code or runtime dependency was imported. Its model-directed result-conditioned search remains an open cross-source candidate under M11-NOV-01; the rejected static-query trials are not evidence that this broader loop cannot work. The clean pinned checkout was removed after release verification. No new public research run was launched for a documentation-only release.

## M11 follow-up: maintained PubMed fixture screen

The [25 September raw-prose screen](sakana/novelty-fixture-discovery-assessment-v1.md) and its [three-call result](sakana/novelty-fixture-discovery-results-v1.json) returned no known target PMID and mostly unrelated first pages. A red-first PubMed-only subject-first query rewrite and bounded selected-rung trace were then tested offline. The separately [preregistered recovery screen](sakana/novelty-fixture-recovery-prereg-v1.json) sent the committed builder's exact queries through the maintained MCP path; its [result](sakana/novelty-fixture-recovery-results-v1.json) and [abstract-level assessment](sakana/novelty-fixture-recovery-assessment-v1.md) show target recall still **0/3**. STMN2 and SARS searches reached an anchored rung and surfaced related but non-supporting papers; Qa-1b fell to an unanchored OR rung and returned unrelated papers. The rewrite was reverted as `6c5072dc` before release. The bounded rung log remains an operational diagnostic. These screens reject that deterministic query rewrite on its declared exact-target metric; they do not evaluate or reject Sakana's model-directed result-conditioned technique, which remains open under the current M11-NOV-01 follow-up items. No model, paid service, product release, or extra repository investigation was used.

A subsequent [diagnosis and preregistered sort pilot](sakana/novelty-retrieval-diagnosis-prereg-v1.md) separates what the screen observed from four possible causes: restrictive query translation, newest-first ESearch ranking, loss of thin precise-rung IDs, and fulltext-first selection from the nine-ID buffer. NCBI documents `pub_date` and `relevance` as different ESearch sorts; neither the retained three-result output nor exploratory searches prove which cause dominated. The next bounded, keyless comparison varies only sort on identical subject-first queries, records all rung and selection IDs, and pairs the three known-prior-art drafts with three distinct scientific controls. This is a fixture-recovery pilot, not adoption or a claim about Google's implementation. The product still uses its original validation query and date sort; M11-NOV-01 remains open until a valid result-conditioned comparison exists.

The [completed 12-call result](sakana/novelty-sort-pilot-results-v1.json) and [blinded abstract assessment](sakana/novelty-sort-pilot-assessment-v1.json) close **M11-NOV-SORT-01**, an **external technique** from NCBI's relevance ordering. Both isolated builds used the same query and maintained MCP tool; the candidate changed only ESearch's sort literal. Exact positive target recall@3 was **0/3 in each arm**. The relevance arm found one mechanism-supporting STMN2 abstract where the date arm found none, but its distinct-control own-anchor recall fell to **1/3** from **2/3**. The primary improvement rule did not pass, so relevance sorting is **not adopted**; the actual product remains on `pub_date`. These abstract judgments are model-assisted triage, not expert validation. All 12 keyless calls completed without a retrieval error or shared-pool carry-over, and no project-model inference or paid call was made. The bounded trace, source hashes, exact served sort, process IDs, and per-call PMID selection are retained; the 36 raw public abstracts were removed after blinded labels and hashes were recorded.

The trace opens **M11-NOV-RUNG-01**, a **local design choice** still under investigation: the SARS endothelial control's exact query found its own prior-art PMID `42150851` on rung 1 in both arms, but the search widened to rung 2 to fill three papers and discarded that precise hit before final selection. This demonstrates loss of a relevant precise-rung hit, not an improvement to any positive case: no positive target appeared in any first-nine rung under either sort. The separate M11-NOV-RUNG-01 [frozen protocol](sakana/novelty-precise-rung-prereg-v1.json) predeclares a bounded six-pair comparison of precise-rung retention, recall, controls and provenance; candidate and runner verification precede any live retrieval. Neither this observation nor the failed sort candidate evaluates Sakana's result-conditioned model-directed loop, which remains open as M11-NOV-01b.

## M11 precise-rung disposition, 26 September 2026

The isolated precise-rung candidate is **rejected for adoption** under its preregistered joint rule. Its separately [frozen confirmation](sakana/novelty-precise-rung-01c1-confirmatory-prereg-v1.json) used three new positive/control pairs outside the earlier B. fragilis, SARS and R01–R06 observations. A [committed authorization amendment](sakana/novelty-precise-rung-01c1-confirmatory-authorization-amendment-2026-09-26.json) preceded the single keyless run. The [sealed result and blind review](sakana/novelty-precise-rung-01c2c-confirmatory-review-2026-09-26.md) completed 12/12 calls, locked 36 abstract labels before unblinding, and preserved build, trace, cache, PMID and cleanup provenance. Exact positive-target PMID recall@3 was **0/3 in both arms**. No positive or control anchor was lost, no request gained unrelated abstracts, and no abstract was insufficient, but the required primary improvement was absent. The prior exploratory comparison's 0→1 signal cannot override a completed confirmatory gate failure. An independent blinded reviewer and a separate score audit used Antigravity Gemini 3.8 Flash High; these model judgments do not establish expert or wet-lab validation.

This rejects only the **local design choice** to retain first-seen PMIDs from already-attempted relaxation rungs under the fixed six-query protocol. It does not reject Sakana's separate result-conditioned model-directed search candidate, which remains open as M11-NOV-01 and awaits a qualified exact-zero model. No Sakana source code or isolated precise-rung runtime change entered the maintained product, so no product release or deployment was made for this disposition. The pinned experimental runner and receipts remain evidence, not a runtime dependency.
